note:
Newcastle Circus on the 1901 census - three households, twenty-six people - read from the enumerator's page and checked by A. Hagues.

**All three are unfiled.** The record keeps five properties on the circus - 2 Newcastle Circus, Mevell House at 7, Burton House, Castlethorpe and Newcastle Court - and two of the three schedules are headed by the street alone. The third is headed **"St John's"**, a name the record has never held anywhere. See [[1901-house-names-not-in-the-record]].

**The St John's household bears on an open question.** It is **Mary Brownsword**, a widow of 65 born at Melbourne in Derbyshire, with her son Arthur, a lace manufacturer and employer of 31, and four servants. Arthur is already in the record as a cousin of Helena Brownsword Dowson, and this gives him a mother and shows her widowed by 1901 - which is the thread [[brownsword-one-family]] has been waiting on.

**Charles Wilfred Birkin's household is the largest on the round here** - twelve people, his wife Clara born in New York, two young daughters, a visiting boy from Ireland and seven servants including two nurses.
source: 1901 census enumerator's page for Newcastle Circus, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
